about.title: Oroville Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast — a wet floor near a checkout line on Oroville Dam Boulevard East, a cracked walkway outside a shop off Olive Highway, poor lighting in a parking lot along Feather River Boulevard. What follows is often confusing: pain, missed work, and a property owner who may not readily admit fault. California law requires showing the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazardous condition and didn't fix or warn of it. That's why acting quickly matters — photos of the hazard, witness names, and store surveillance footage can disappear or get overwritten within days. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect people in Oroville who've been hurt in a fall with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate the details and explain your options. There's no cost to get matched, and any attorney you work with is paid only if your claim results in a recovery. You focus on healing — we handle finding the right point of contact.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Premises Law

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires proof the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that speak to notice.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Oroville businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having nothing.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if a property owner argues you weren't watching where you stepped, California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover a reduced amount rather than nothing at all.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Oroville?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the fall to file a claim, though it can be shorter if a government-owned property, like a city sidewalk or public building, is involved. Missing that window typically ends your ability to pursue compensation. It's best to have an attorney check the specifics of your situation as soon as possible.

items.question: What if the fall happened in a parking lot along Feather River Boulevard or Oroville Dam Boulevard?
items.answer: Parking lots are common fall sites due to uneven pavement, potholes, or poor lighting, and they're still subject to the same premises liability rules. An attorney would look at who owns or maintains the lot and whether they had notice of the condition. Photos of the specific spot, taken as soon as possible, can help support the claim.

items.question: Do I need proof the store or property owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: Yes — under California law, you generally need to show the owner knew or should have known about the dangerous condition and failed to address it. This is often shown through prior complaints, cleaning logs, or how long the hazard existed before your fall. An independent attorney can help identify what evidence applies to your specific claim.
